articles.title: Angel Reese, Dream Beat Valkyries in WNBA Finals Game 2, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Top Players
articles.summary: Home-court advantage in the 2026 WNBA Finals now belongs to the Atlanta Dream.
articles.body:
Home-court advantage in the 2026 WNBA Finals now belongs to the Atlanta Dream.

Angel Reese and the Dream came into the Chase Center on Monday and left with a commanding 79-65 victory over the Golden State Valkyries in Game 2 to tie the series at one apiece.

The Dream have plenty of momentum as the series shifts to Atlanta in large part because of Reese's individual brilliance during a historic performance. She was unguardable down low, dominant on the boards and her usual self on defense, while Allisha Gray provided important scoring as well.

Enes Kanter Freedom Says He Will Attend WNBA Finals Game 3 in Atlanta (AP)

Golden State was unable to overcome Gabby Williams' shooting struggles (3-of-15 from the field) and had no answer for the visitors.

Game 1 was a defensive battle with the Valkyries taking over in crunch time and limiting the Dream to a mere eight points in the fourth quarter. That put the Atlanta offense firmly under the spotlight for Game 2 since it could have stolen one on the road with even an average offensive performance at the end of that first contest.

And the visitors responded in the early going by taking a two-point halftime lead.

Reese matched those eight points in the first quarter by herself and had 15 at intermission by doing a little bit of everything. She got out in transition, created opportunities in half-court sets with her rim-running and finished through contact all while battling for boards and protecting the rim on the defensive side.

Her initial impact was particularly important because Rhyne Howard picked up her fourth foul in the second quarter. That put more of the onus on everyone else, and Gray also helped carry the offense by hitting from the outside when defenders collapsed on Reese in the paint.

Still, Golden State was well within striking distance with Tiffany Hayes providing a spark off the bench to help make up for Williams' shooting woes as the star did much of her scoring from the free-throw line.

But striking distance disappeared during the first real separation of the game when Atlanta closed the third quarter on a 15-2 run.

Reese was the driving force behind the spurt with six of the points, an assist and a steal, but it was Jordin Canada who added the exclamation mark by banking in a long-range three as time expired.

Atlanta's defense was also not to be overlooked, as it held the Valkyries to a paltry nine points in the quarter. Williams couldn't get anything going after playing so well in Game 1, which stifled nearly everything Golden State tried on the offensive side.

The fourth quarter was largely a formality with the Dream in full control, although it was fitting it was Reese who hit a three with fewer than five minutes remaining to push the advantage back to 19 after Golden State built slight momentum.

She was the best player on the floor and took over whenever needed for a team that will now return home for an important Game 3 on Wednesday.

articles.title: 'I Was Hungry,' Angel Reese Reacts to Historic Performance in Dream Win vs. Valkyries in WNBA Finals
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream's Game 1 loss to the Golden State Valkyries in the 2026 WNBA Finals was a motivating factor for Angel Reese in Monday's 79-65 victory in Game 2.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Dream's Game 1 loss to the Golden State Valkyries in the 2026 WNBA Finals was a motivating factor for Angel Reese in Monday's 79-65 victory in Game 2.

"I was hungry," she told reporters after leading the Dream to their first WNBA Finals win in franchise history (36:40 mark). "I wanted one. I think we let one slip away. And you can't do that, especially on the road in a good environment against a good team.

"We all came together and were pissed. We felt disappointed. We felt embarrassed. We didn't like the outcome of that last game, and we didn't want to let another one slip."

Enes Kanter Freedom Says He Will Attend WNBA Finals Game 3 in Atlanta (AP)

Atlanta led Game 1 by five points heading into the fourth quarter but managed to score just eight total points in the last quarter as Golden State earned the win.

There would be no such missed opportunities for the visitors in Game 2, though, as they finished the third quarter on a 15-2 run to seize a double-digit advantage and never looked back during a fourth quarter that ended up being largely a formality.

Reese was the driving force behind the win and finished with 30 points, 16 rebounds, three assists and two blocks in a dominant performance.

She joined Breanna Stewart and Jonquel Jones as the only players in WNBA history to finish with 30 or more points and 15 or more rebounds in a Finals game. The Dream turned to her whenever they needed a basket all while she provided her normal stifling defense on the other end.

The LSU product got out in transition, scored on the blocks and even hit a three-pointer in the fourth quarter as Atlanta turned away any late spurts from the Valkyries.

It wasn't just Reese, as Allisha Gray drilled three triples on her way to 18 points. Jordin Canada added 13 points, three of which came on a banked three-pointer to end that decisive third quarter.

The Atlanta defense also set the tone and held Gabby Williams to 3-of-15 shooting from the field. Golden State as a whole shot an ugly 34 percent from the field with 18 turnovers and failed to generate enough open looks to keep pace with Reese's unstoppable performance.

Now the series shifts to Atlanta for Wednesday's Game 3 with all the momentum on the Dream's side thanks in large part to Reese.

articles.body: Las Atlanta Dream doblegaron a las Golden State Valkyries por 65-79 en el segundo juego de las finales de la WNBA, impulsadas por una brillante actuación de Angel Reese en el Chase Center de San Francisco, en el estado de California, que empata la serie. Las Valkyries dominaron por la mínima (21-18) el primer tramo del encuentro frente a unas Dream impulsadas por la intensidad de la estadounidense Angel Reese, quien aportó ocho puntos clave y que acabó el partido como la máxima anotadora con 30 puntos (16 de 10 en tiro). Sin embargo, al término de la primera mitad, la balanza se inclinó por 37-39 a favor del conjunto de las de Atlanta, que tomaron la delantera aprovechando un flojo desempeño ofensivo de las de San Francisco, que registraron un 23 % de efectividad en tiros de campo. El conjunto del este de Estados Unidos intensificó el ritmo en el tercer parcial y estiró la diferencia hasta los doce puntos en los últimos suspiros. Tras el descanso, las Dream consolidaron la brecha aprovechando una falta sobre Reese y un espectacular triple sobre la bocina de Jordin Canada que dejó el marcador en 46-60 al término del periodo. El equipo visitante mantuvo el control del juego gracias a una sólida efectividad desde la línea de tiros libres, que alcanzó el 100 %, contrastando con las dificultades ofensivas de las californianas. Reese se echó al equipo en el último cuarto para seguir agrandando las distancias frente en el último cuarto, con una diferencia de 14 puntos que mantiene en vivo la competición por el título más grande la WNBA y dejó sin contestación a las de California en su propio territorio. Las Valkyries ganaron el primer asalto por un ajustado 68-64 que se disputó el pasado sábado en San Francisco. articles.summary: Atlanta Dream win their first ever game in the WNBA Finals as they beat the Golden State Valkyries 79-65 to level the series at 1-1.
articles.body:
Atlanta Dream won their first ever game in the WNBA Finals as they beat the Golden State Valkyries 79-65 to level the series at 1-1.

Angel Reese scored 30 points and grabbed 16 rebounds as the Dream condemned the Valkyries to a defeat in front of their fans in San Francisco.

The Georgia franchise held a 39-37 half-time lead and took control of the match in a 13-minute spell spanning the third and fourth quarter, adding 30 points while only conceding eight in return.

Reese scored nine of her points in that period and becomes only the third player to reach 30 points and 15 rebounds in a Finals series, following Jonquel Jones in 2019 and Breanna Stewart in 2020.

The 24-year-old, who is in her first season with the Dream after being traded from the Chicago Sky, is also the youngest player to reach the landmark in a WNBA post-season match.

"She just came out on a mission tonight," said defensive guard Allisha Gray of her team-mate.

The Dream had lost the match of the series 68-64 on Saturday, and Reese - the league's defensive player of the year - said she was keen to make amends for her performance in that game.

"I let my team down last game, not really contributing as much as I could in the second half," said Reese.

"I just wanted to make sure I came out tonight and left my mark. And I think I did that.

"I was hungry, I think we let one slip away [on Saturday]. You can't do that. We felt disappointed, we felt embarrassed.

"I walked off the court not feeling like myself, and I wanted to make sure that, this game, I did everything I could do to walk off the court and feel like who I am."

The Dream had previously had a record of zero wins and 10 defeats in the Finals, following 3-0 series defeats in 2010, 2011 and 2013.

After two matches in California, the best-of-seven series now switches to Atlanta, where games three and four will be played on Thursday, 22 October and Saturday, 24 October.

articles.title: NBA: LeBron James' Philadelphia 76ers face vital litmus test against reigning champion New York Knicks on opening night
articles.summary: LeBron James' Philadelphia 76ers face reigning champion New York Knicks in a blockbuster Madison Square Garden clash to open 2026/27 season; watch all of NBA opening night live on Sky Sports, starting with Boston Celtics vs Detroit Pistons from 8pm on Sky Sports +
articles.body:
One of the greatest players in the sport's history in LeBron James will make his 76ers debut alongside a plethora of other superstars in a new-look Philadelphia side that visit the title holders - New York Knicks - at Madison Square Garden, live on Sky Sports Main Event from 11pm on Tuesday.

It doesn't get any bigger than this to begin a new season.

Much of the off-season discussion has centred around James' move to the east coast and the threat his Sixers side could pose to existing title contenders.

That is talk that a stacked Knicks team will be hoping to prove is cheap at the very first opportunity in front of what is set to be a raucous New York crowd, with the home side set to hoist the Larry O'Brien trophy in front of their fans pre-match after winning their first championship in 53 years.

So - is Philadelphia's drastic off-season rebuild actually enough to give them true title credentials? Or are the Knicks still in pole position to retain the NBA championship?

We assess the state of play in the Eastern Conference heading into the blockbuster match that opens the new NBA season...

The optimism in Philadelphia in May was palpable after Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey led the Sixers to a famous game seven victory on the road against the second seed Boston Celtics.

They secured a remarkable 4-3 first-round win after coming from 3-1 down, their first post-season series win against their fierce rivals since 1982.

Their joy was short-lived. The eventual champion Knicks made quick work of the Sixers, winning four out of four to secure the series sweep and condemn them to yet another second-round exit - a stage of the playoffs they have not been able to progress past in seven attempts since 2001.

That record is what James' side will be hoping to change. His addition gives the Sixers a formidable starting five featuring all-star point guard Tyrese Maxey, promising second-year wing VJ Edgecombe, and another headline addition in the NBA's leading scorer Jaylen Brown, who arrives after a blockbuster summer trade that saw the Sixers give up Paul George and draft picks in return.

The frontcourt of superstars James and Joel Embiid boasts an incredible level of NBA acumen, with five NBA MVP awards between them.

"I didn't leave my family [in Los Angeles] to lose in the second round," James said on the Sixers' pre-season media day. "I know that for sure. Work needs to be done, and I'm ready to get to work."

The key to their success will be whether head coach Nick Nurse can find a sense of balance in a starting five that features four players averaging over 20 points a night.

A 42-year-old James has already embraced the change from scorer to facilitator in his older years. After the Lakers' playoff defeat to the Thunder, he told a press conference that it was "pretty cool" to play as the third scoring option for his former team in 2025/26.

He looks set to continue that transition in a team with three of the NBA's top 10 scorers from last season.

The biggest challenge for Philadelphia will come on the defensive side of the ball. While Edgecombe solidified his status as a defender of significant calibre in his rookie season, each of the other four starters are more offensive-minded - meaning at least one will have to put himself forward to take on the more challenging defensive match-ups.

They will need to find that balance fast against a multi-faceted Knicks offence - otherwise, the NBA's newest 'super team' could find itself with more questions than answers at the start of a crucial campaign.

The Knicks, in many ways, are an example of the opposite path to success than their opening-day opponents are attempting to follow.

Their championship run was the result of a roster built over multiple years, prioritising significant depth and a team-first underdog mentality epitomised by star Jalen Brunson, who himself was passed on by multiple teams in the draft - and free agency in years past - due to doubts over his physical attributes.

The spine of their championship-winning side also boasts a level of familiarity that is the envy of much of the NBA. Three of their core players - Brunson, guard Josh Hart and forward Mikal Bridges - won a national championship together at college level with Villanova, and are entering their third season on the same NBA team.

That championship-level chemistry - that the Knicks built from the ground up - is what the Sixers will be hoping to establish with their newly acquired superstars in just a fraction of the time.

New York's off-season activity prioritised continuity, retaining three of the four team members eligible for free agency and making just one signing: that of former Sixers centre Andre Drummond on a veteran's minimum deal, replacing Mitchell Robinson after he was poached on a three-year, $47.4m (£35.6m) contract by the Celtics.

Robinson's loss is a significant one, but retaining the services of 10 of the 11 core players in a championship-winning side conveys a clear message: they believe in their championship-winning formula, and are hungry for more.

"We're all excited for the opportunity to do it again," Hart told reporters on media day. "You guys will see that with how we conduct ourselves and how we play, that we're not satisfied with one."

Recording an opening-night win and maintaining the status quo against a team who have been the off-season talk of the league would make a clear statement - one that could help determine the course of the Eastern Conference throughout the rest of the season.

DREAM, VALKYRIES SKIP NATIONAL ANTHEM IN WNBA FINALS GAME 2 DESPITE RULEBOOK REQUIREMENT It took four trips to the Finals for the Dream to finally win a game. Atlanta was swept in 2010, 2011 and 2013, then lost Saturday’s opener to fall to 0-10 in championship series games. Reese helped put an end to that streak with one of the best games of her career. But before tipoff, there was another national anthem controversy. Both teams again stayed off the court for the anthem, leaving the floor just before the start of the "Star-Spangled Banner" and returning seconds after Alanis Morissette finished her performance. The WNBA’s rulebook calls for players, coaches and trainers to stand and line up during the anthem. The league has not answered OutKick’s questions about the teams’ absences. Once the game began, Reese attacked the basket and kept giving Atlanta offense. She scored eight points in the first quarter and seven in the second, giving her 15 points on 6-of-9 shooting in the first half. Those 15 points represented one more than she scored in all of Game 1. ANGEL REESE IS IN THE WNBA FINALS, BUT HER CHICAGO EXIT RAISES QUESTIONS ABOUT HER WINNING MENTALITY Reese’s strong night still included a brief tantrum early in the third quarter. With the game tied at 40, she stomped her feet after not getting the ball and walked away while Atlanta’s possession continued, taking herself out of position to pursue an offensive rebound. That’s a bad look in a Finals game. To Reese's credit, she didn't let one bad moment define her night. She followed the outburst with a block on Tiffany Hayes, then later finished through contact against Kiah Stokes and completed the three-point play. Cameras showed Reese yelling "Give me the f-----g ball!" after the and-1 bucket. Reese finished with nine third-quarter points, matching Golden State’s entire output. The Valkyries never made Reese pay for entering the second half with three fouls. She stayed on the floor for the entire third quarter without picking up another one, while Golden State kept firing jump shots and failed to get to the free-throw line. Both teams made four field goals in the third quarter, including one three-pointer apiece. Atlanta went 12-for-12 at the foul line. Golden State didn’t attempt a free throw. This wasn't a case of a one-way whistle, either; Golden State routinely settled for outside shots rather than attacking the paint. Reese added six points in the fourth quarter, including a 24-foot three-pointer that put Atlanta ahead 74-55 with 4:15 remaining. The series moves to Atlanta’s State Farm Arena for Game 3 on Wednesday.

articles.title: El caso Aday Mara: mejor jugar que litigar
articles.summary: La opinión de Jesús Sánchez
articles.body: Es posible que cuando pase el tiempo se recuerde el 20 de octubre de 2026 como la fecha del debut de Aday Mara en la NBA. Sin duda, el pívot de 2,21 y 21 años es el jugador más ilusionante que ha dado el baloncesto español en los últimos tiempos, un 'unicornio' por su singularidad (sus características físicas y técnicas), un gigante que recuerda a los hermanos Gasol, por tamaño, clase y finura. Las comparaciones con los 'totem' no le hacen ningún bien, salvo que se lo tome como un estímulo, pero es placentero volver a pisar el territorio de los sueños. Aday parece el hombre destinado a cerrar en la selección la puerta de la nostalgia. Está llamado a liderar una generación de jugadores jóvenes con enormes posibilidades en los próximos años. Aday va a poder jugar con los Thunder en San Antonio en su primer partido oficial. No sobra recordarlo. El Baloncesto Zaragoza le denunció en su día por incumplimiento de contrato y esgrime que es jugador suyo, aunque no viste de rojo desde mayor de 2023. Sostiene que Mara no pagó cláusula ninguna para liberarse. Está en su derecho de hacerlo, pero hacerlo en este contexto, en un momento tan significativo y esperanzador para el baloncesto español, chirría. Ese partido se está jugando en otra pista y quizá el Baloncesto Zaragoza saque un buen resultado. O no. También se podría debatir si es moralmente lícito exigir una cláusula de 700.000 euros a un jugador que cobraba auténtica 'calderilla': 600.000 euros brutos por siete temporadas. Para alguien que siente tanto al Zaragoza, que lleva tres años compitiendo en la NCAA sin problemas (a efectos del 'transfer' su club de procedencia, por llamarlo así, es Michigan Wolverines) y que ha deslumbrado en la pretemporada con los Thunder, amenazarle con tantos decibelios con impedirle debutar en la NBA (el sueño de cualquier jugador de baloncesto) quizá sea legítimo legalmente pero queda feo. Reabrir el conflicto ahora no tocaba. A Aday no le hace falta el famoso transfer para jugar con los Thunder, como ya han dicho en la franquicia que fue campeona en 2025. El caso lleva su curso en los tribunales y allí se resolverá cuál es la naturaleza de su relación con el Zaragoza y el montante económico de la cláusula liberatoria. ¿A quién beneficia tanto fango? A nadie. Por la salud de todos, deberían llegar a un acuerdo amistoso. El Zaragoza defiende sus intereses pero ¿no sería mejor presumir de él que llevarle al juzgado? Y, por otro lado, seguro que a Aday no le interesa este ruido. En la cancha, lo importante, Mara, con el que conviene ir transitando poco a poco sin renunciar a anhelar un crecimiento acorde a su fantástica dimensión como jugador, ha tenido la fortuna de acabar en Oklahoma City, donde se desarrolla bien el talento joven; donde, bien arropado, no tendrá demasiada carga; donde puede ser una alternativa (ofreciendo otras posibilidades de juego, poste bajo y mejor pase generador) a Holmgren y Hartenstein. Ha trabajado muy bien en verano y ha tenido partidos en pretemporada de extraordinaria efectividad, respondiendo a las expectativas y a la fascinación que habían ofrecido su enorme talla (en muchos sentidos), su puesto número 12 en el Draft y su último año universitario, coronado con el histórico título. Seguramente no le hace bien que le cataloguen de posible AntiWembanyama y al mismo tiempo es halagador estar en esta conversación con temática marciana. El baloncesto español, que también saluda para la NBA a Baba Miller (otro jugador muy especial que debe ser capital para la selección) y a Sergio de Larrea (también ha aterrizado en la competición profesional de pie), que tiene a Hugo bien posicionado en Boston en el siempre difícil segundo año, que espera que Santi Aldama supere sus problemas físicos e inicia una nueva singladura deportiva con los Mavericks, tiene en Mara su primer gran proyecto de estrella NBA en años. Celebrémoslo. Mejor jugar que litigar.

articles.title: El circuito 3x3 CaixaBank 2026 bate récord de asistencia
articles.standfirst: Su temporada más inclusiva y abierta a la ciudadanía: ha congregado a más de 5.000 jugadores y jugadoras de todas las edades y ha alcanzado los 115.000 asistentes totales
articles.summary: Su temporada más inclusiva y abierta a la ciudadanía: ha congregado a más de 5.000 jugadores y jugadoras de todas las edades y ha alcanzado los 115.000 asistentes totales
articles.body: La temporada de 2026 del Circuito 3x3 CaixaBank ha concluido con unas cifras de récord en términos de participación y asistencia, siendo el año que más visitantes totales ha acumulado. Un total de 115.000 asistentes han acudido a alguna de las once paradas de la temporada, once ciudades que han sido testigo del mejor baloncesto gratuito y al aire libre. La primera semana de octubre se cerró en Málaga una temporada que comenzó en Madrid, a finales de abril. El Circuito 3x3 CaixaBank 2026 también ha pasado por San Fernando, Vigo, Salamanca, Santander, Vitoria, Pamplona, Guadalajara, Cáceres y Valladolid. Un total de once ciudades que, además de batir el récord histórico de visitantes acumulado, han contado con un total de 5.407 jugadores y jugadoras de los 1.262 equipos inscritos, que ha disputado 2.039 partidos. El Circuito cierra así su edición más inclusiva y abierta a toda la ciudadanía, una temporada récord gracias su carácter social, que ha ofrecido mucho más que baloncesto en todas las ciudades a las que ha llegado y ha consolidado su misión de hacer el baloncesto más accesible y de acercar los valores del deporte al conjunto de la sociedad. Con esta decimocuarta edición, El Circuito 3x3 CaixaBank alcanza las 154 paradas itinerantes desde que arrancó en 2012. Y desde su primera edición, el Circuito 3x3 CaixaBank suma unos registros totales que se acercan a los 70.000 participantes y alcanzan los 590.000 visitantes acumulados. Unas cifras que ratifican su valor como el mayor circuito de baloncesto 3x3 gratuito y al aire libre de España. Por tercer año consecutivo, la iniciativa #MárcateUnTripleSolidario se ha consolidado como uno de los grandes emblemas sociales del circuito. En cada una de las sedes, tanto participantes como autoridades, embajadores y público visitante han vuelto a cumplir con el reto de alcanzar los 1.000 triples solidarios por parada. Cada canasta se ha traducido nuevamente en una ayuda económica directa de la Fundación "la Caixa" a favor de entidades y asociaciones locales comprometidas con la inclusión y la igualdad de oportunidades en cada municipio. En esta edición de 2026, los casi 15.000 triples anotados a lo largo de la gira han permitido canalizar recursos decisivos hacia proyectos de transformación social de ámbito local. De este modo, el circuito refuerza el valor del baloncesto no solo como disciplina deportiva y de ocio urbano, sino como una herramienta transversal capaz de generar un impacto positivo y duradero en la sociedad. Bajo el lema ‘Juega y vive el baloncesto’, la temporada 2026 del Circuito 3x3 CaixaBank ha querido ir un paso más allá en su propuesta, trasladando el mensaje de que el baloncesto no solo se practica en la pista, sino que se comparte y se disfruta fuera de ella gracias a sus valores de esfuerzo, respeto, superación y trabajo en equipo. A lo largo de la gira, las pistas no solo han albergado partidos, sino que han acogido un abanico de actividades pensadas para el público general: dinámicas de envejecimiento activo entre los más mayores para incentivar una vida más activa, juegos participativos para familias y actividades para los más jóvenes. Esa fusión entre deporte y cultura ha tenido además su máxima expresión artística en el proyecto Basket & Art, una iniciativa que ha recogido 11 grafitis elaborados a lo largo de la gira y que han sido expuestos en la parada final de Málaga, luciendo en un entorno icónico ante el Centre Pompidou como muestra viva del arte urbano y el espíritu de este circuito.
